===== WORLD 17 · LESSON value_and_bluff · Value and bluff =====

TASK w17_1_teach [theory] Two reasons to re-raise
CAPTION: A 3-bet re-raises an opening raise. A value 3-bet means re-raising to collect money from weaker hands. A light 3-bet relies more on folds and may retain equity when called.
TEACH: Two reasons to re-raise A 3-bet re-raises an opening raise. A value 3-bet means re-raising to collect money from weaker hands. A light 3-bet relies more on folds and may retain equity when called.
Q: What distinguishes a value 3-bet from a light 3-bet?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Which worse hands pay and how much the play depends on folds — Correct. Look through the opener’s continue range. The position and size are inputs to that comparison.
  - [wrong] Whether the re-raise wins immediately — Look again. A value 3-bet can take down the pot preflop. The classification is about the reason it earns money.
    BETTER ANSWER: Which worse hands pay and how much the play depends on folds
  - [wrong] Whether a pocket pair is involved — Look again. Pairs span weak and strong holdings. The response range decides what can continue.
    BETTER ANSWER: Which worse hands pay and how much the play depends on folds

TASK w17_1_read_blocked_aces [drill] How many AA combos remain?
CAPTION: CO opened. The premium 4-bet group being studied includes AA and AKo. Count how many of its AA combinations remain when your A♠ is known.
Q: How many AA combos remain?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You As 4s | Pot 4 BB | To call 2.5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO stack 97.5 BB raise 2.5 BB | BTN dealer As 4s stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ folds · preflop: CO raises to 2.5 BB
  + [correct] 3 combos — Correct. One known ace leaves three aces. Pairing any two of those gives three combinations.
  - [wrong] 4 combos — Look again. Four is the original number of aces. The pair count comes from choosing two.
    BETTER ANSWER: 3 combos
  - [wrong] 6 combos — Look again. Six is the count before any ace is blocked.
    BETTER ANSWER: 3 combos

TASK w17_1_guided_choose_value_job [drill] Which action charges the stated weaker calls before the flop?
CAPTION: CO opens 2.5 BB. CO will call a BTN 3-bet to 8 BB with QQ JJ TT AQs AKo and re-raise AA. The exercise asks which available action offers a preflop value re-raise.
TEACH: Which action charges the stated weaker calls before the flop? A value 3-bet has to collect from something. Name the hands paying the extra chips.
Q: Which action charges the stated weaker calls before the flop?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You Kh Kd | Pot 4 BB | To call 2.5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts pocket pair
EFFECTIVE: CO 100 · SB 100 · BB 100
REASONING: principle three_bet_jobs · alt alternative · edge moreValueFromWorse · stack_matters false · assumption none
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO stack 97.5 BB raise 2.5 BB | BTN dealer Kh Kd stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ folds · preflop: CO raises to 2.5 BB
  + [correct] 3-bet to 8 BB — Correct. Re-raise because CO calls with queens, jacks, tens and weaker broadways. Calling misses those extra payments; AA’s re-raise is a separate decision.
  - [wrong] Call 2.5 BB — Look again. A call can retain weaker opens. It does not collect the listed re-raise payments.
    BETTER ANSWER: 3-bet to 8 BB
  - [wrong] Fold — Look again. Folding refuses every contribution and forfeits the chance to charge weaker hands.
    BETTER ANSWER: 3-bet to 8 BB

TASK w17_1_transfer_select_bluff_candidate [drill] Which candidate removes more of the specified 4-bet range and retains a flush possibility?
CAPTION: HJ opened, CO folded, and BTN acts. Compare your A♠5♠ with the offsuit hand in the choices as light 3-bet candidates. The stated opener folds some medium hands and can 4-bet AA or AKo.
Q: Which candidate removes more of the specified 4-bet range and retains a flush possibility?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You As 5s | Pot 4 BB | To call 2.5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ stack 97.5 BB raise 2.5 BB | CO folded stack 100 BB | BTN dealer As 5s stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ raises to 2.5 BB · preflop: CO folds
  + [correct] A♠5♠ — Correct. The ace removes three AA and three AKo. Two spades also keep the possibility of making a flush.
  - [wrong] 7♣4♦ — Look again. Neither card removes any AA or AKo. The two ranks also start offsuit and disconnected.
    BETTER ANSWER: A♠5♠
  - [wrong] They achieve the same removal — Look again. Both aces and kings are still fully available against 7-4. A-5 removes an ace.
    BETTER ANSWER: A♠5♠

TASK w17_1_day7_light_bluff_signal [review] What undermines a 3-bet that relies on making better hands fold?
ENTRY: drill
CAPTION: BTN faces a CO open. Against a re-raise this CO keeps almost every better ace, every strong broadway and every pair. CO mostly folds weaker suited trash.
Q: What undermines a 3-bet that relies on making better hands fold?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You Qc 9c | Pot 4 BB | To call 2.5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO stack 97.5 BB raise 2.5 BB | BTN dealer Qc 9c stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ folds · preflop: CO raises to 2.5 BB
  + [correct] Most of the range that beats Q-9 continues — Correct. The folds are concentrated in hands Q-9 is already ahead of. Better hands usually stay and charge a large price.
  - [wrong] Q-9 is suited — Look again. Holding two cards of the same suit can help equity when called. It does not determine which better hands fold.
    BETTER ANSWER: Most of the range that beats Q-9 continues
  - [wrong] BTN would be in position — Look again. Position can help after a call. It does not supply immediate folds.
    BETTER ANSWER: Most of the range that beats Q-9 continues

===== WORLD 17 · LESSON position_and_squeeze · Position and squeeze =====

TASK w17_2_teach [theory] Re-raising after a caller
CAPTION: A flat call means matching the raise without raising again. A cold call is a call of a raise by a player who has not voluntarily entered. A squeeze is a re-raise after an opener and one or more callers. Heads-up means two players remain. A 3-bet pot is a pot in which the preflop re-raise was matched. The dead money is the reward if they fold. Players behind can still affect the result.
TEACH: Re-raising after a caller A flat call means matching the raise without raising again. A cold call is a call of a raise by a player who has not voluntarily entered. A squeeze is a re-raise after an opener and one or more callers. Heads-up means two players remain. A 3-bet pot is a pot in which the preflop re-raise was matched. The dead money is the reward if they fold. Players behind can still affect the result.
Q: Which sequence creates an opportunity to squeeze?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Raise, call, then a re-raise — Correct. The cold caller’s chips add to the pot and give the re-raiser another range to get through.
  - [wrong] Raise then re-raise with nobody calling — Look again. This is an ordinary heads-up 3-bet opportunity. No flat call came between the raises.
    BETTER ANSWER: Raise, call, then a re-raise
  - [wrong] Two limps before an opening raise — Look again. The first raise remains the opening raise. The limpers have not called a raise.
    BETTER ANSWER: Raise, call, then a re-raise

TASK w17_2_read_squeeze_price [drill] What is in the pot before BTN decides?
CAPTION: HJ opens to 2.5 BB, CO calls and BTN acts. The two blinds have posted and have yet to respond.
Q: What is in the pot before BTN decides?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You Ac Qd | Pot 6.5 BB | To call 2.5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ stack 97.5 BB raise 2.5 BB | CO stack 97.5 BB | BTN dealer Ac Qd stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ raises to 2.5 BB · preflop: CO calls 2.5 BB
  + [correct] 6.5 BB — Correct. Both 2.5 BB contributions and the 1.5 BB of blinds are already committed.
  - [wrong] 5 BB — Look again. This counts the open and call only. The blinds are already in the pot.
    BETTER ANSWER: 6.5 BB
  - [wrong] 9 BB — Look again. This adds another 2.5 BB before BTN has made a decision.
    BETTER ANSWER: 6.5 BB

TASK w17_2_guided_size_oop [drill] Which size offers CO the worse immediate price?
CAPTION: CO opens 2.5 BB; BTN and SB fold. BB can re-raise to 8 or 11 BB. If CO calls, there is 0.5 BB in dead small blind. Compare the caller’s two preflop prices.
TEACH: Which size offers CO the worse immediate price? Use the opponent’s remaining call amount and the pot after that call.
Q: Which size offers CO the worse immediate price?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You Ah Qh | Pot 4 BB | To call 1.5 BB | Seat BB | Active bb | Decision bb | Facts no applicable hand facts
EFFECTIVE: CO 100
REASONING: principle squeeze_with_dead_money · alt alternative · edge processRule · stack_matters false · assumption none
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO stack 97.5 BB raise 2.5 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB Ah Qh stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ folds · preflop: CO raises to 2.5 BB · preflop: BTN folds · preflop: SB folds
  + [correct] Re-raise to 11 BB — Correct. Raise to 11 BB rather than 8 BB because if CO calls, CO pays 8.5 BB instead of 5.5 BB, a larger share of the final pot.
  - [wrong] Re-raise to 8 BB — Look again. Raise to 8 BB gives CO a smaller amount and percentage to call than a raise to 11 BB.
    BETTER ANSWER: Re-raise to 11 BB
  - [wrong] The prices are equal — Look again. The fixed opening contribution and small blind mean the price does change with the re-raise.
    BETTER ANSWER: Re-raise to 11 BB

TASK w17_2_transfer_squeeze_all_fold [drill] Under that pure-bluff stress test, does the squeeze beat folding?
CAPTION: HJ opened 2.5 BB, CO called, and BTN acts. BTN would add 9 BB. An outcome means one possible result. In ten mutually exclusive, equal-weight results, all remaining players fold in five. In five, somebody continues and the re-raise has zero recovery.
Q: Under that pure-bluff stress test, does the squeeze beat folding?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You Ad 5d | Pot 6.5 BB | To call 2.5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ stack 97.5 BB raise 2.5 BB | CO stack 97.5 BB | BTN dealer Ad 5d stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ raises to 2.5 BB · preflop: CO calls 2.5 BB
  + [correct] Fold. The model loses 1.25 BB for the squeeze — Correct. Five wins of 6.5 BB fail to cover five losses of 9 BB. The stress test excludes showdown recovery.
  - [wrong] Squeeze. It earns 1.25 BB — Look again. The loss in a failed squeeze exceeds the gain when everyone folds.
    BETTER ANSWER: Fold. The model loses 1.25 BB for the squeeze
  - [wrong] The two actions tie — Look again. A half-and-half split ties only if the current pot and risk are equal.
    BETTER ANSWER: Fold. The model loses 1.25 BB for the squeeze

===== WORLD 17 · LESSON defense_and_coverage · Defense and coverage =====

TASK w17_3_teach [theory] What does an opening raiser’s flat call of a 3-bet create?
CAPTION: The opener can fold, call or 4-bet when re-raised. A call retains the 3-bet pot. A player who never entered and calls the 3-bet makes a cold call.
TEACH: What does an opening raiser’s flat call of a 3-bet create? The opener can fold, call or 4-bet when re-raised. A call retains the 3-bet pot. A player who never entered and calls the 3-bet makes a cold call.
Q: What does an opening raiser’s flat call of a 3-bet create?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] A 3-bet pot with the opener defending by calling — Correct. The raise size stands because it was matched. This call comes from a player who already raised.
  - [wrong] A single-raised pot — Look again. The caller did not undo the re-raise. Both players match its total.
    BETTER ANSWER: A 3-bet pot with the opener defending by calling
  - [wrong] A cold call by a new player — Look again. A cold caller would be entering after the two raises with no voluntary chips already committed.
    BETTER ANSWER: A 3-bet pot with the opener defending by calling

TASK w17_3_read_cold_call_identity [drill] Whose call would be cold?
CAPTION: HJ raises to 2.5 BB and CO makes it 8 BB. BTN has no voluntary contribution yet. HJ has not responded to the 3-bet.
Q: Whose call would be cold?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You Jc Jd | Pot 12 BB | To call 8 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts pocket pair
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ stack 97.5 BB raise 2.5 BB | CO stack 92 BB raise 8 BB | BTN dealer Jc Jd stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ raises to 2.5 BB · preflop: CO raises to 8 BB
  + [correct] BTN calling 8 BB — Correct. BTN has not yet entered. The call matches a raise and a re-raise.
  - [wrong] HJ calling the extra 5.5 BB — Look again. HJ already opened, so that is an opener defending a 3-bet.
    BETTER ANSWER: BTN calling 8 BB
  - [wrong] Either call lowers the pot to a single raise — Look again. The 3-bet amount stays live if matched.
    BETTER ANSWER: BTN calling 8 BB

===== WORLD 17 · LESSON four_bet_and_stack · Four bet and stack =====

TASK w17_4_teach [theory] When can an ace blocker support a light 4-bet?
CAPTION: Fold equity means the value gained when opponents fold. Blockers are the cards you hold that reduce the number of possible opposing hands. A 4-bet can collect calls from worse or use fold equity. Depth also determines how much the next all-in costs.
TEACH: When can an ace blocker support a light 4-bet? Fold equity means the value gained when opponents fold. Blockers are the cards you hold that reduce the number of possible opposing hands. A 4-bet can collect calls from worse or use fold equity. Depth also determines how much the next all-in costs.
Q: When can an ace blocker support a light 4-bet?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] When it reduces value continues and enough remaining hands fold — Correct. Removal can lower the chance of running into premiums. The rest of the opponent’s response still governs EV.
  - [wrong] Whenever that card is an ace — Look again. An ace alone does not generate folds or create a profitable payoff after a call.
    BETTER ANSWER: When it reduces value continues and enough remaining hands fold
  - [wrong] When the 4-bet matches the 3-bet rather than increasing it — Look again. A 4-bet raises above the existing re-raise. Matching it is calling.
    BETTER ANSWER: When it reduces value continues and enough remaining hands fold

TASK w17_4_read_four_bet_additional_cost [drill] How many additional BB does CO risk above the chips already paid?
CAPTION: CO opens to 2.5 BB and BTN 3-bets to 8 BB. The blinds fold. CO considers making it 21 BB.
Q: How many additional BB does CO risk above the chips already paid?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You As 4s | Pot 12 BB | To call 5.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO As 4s stack 97.5 BB raise 2.5 BB | BTN dealer stack 92 BB raise 8 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB folded stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ folds · preflop: CO raises to 2.5 BB · preflop: BTN raises to 8 BB · preflop: SB folds · preflop: BB folds
  + [correct] 18.5 BB — Correct. CO already put 2.5 BB in. A raise to 21 BB brings its total to that amount.
  - [wrong] 21 BB — Look again. That is the total raise size, including sunk chips.
    BETTER ANSWER: 18.5 BB
  - [wrong] 13 BB — Look again. That would be a BTN call amount if CO made the 4-bet.
    BETTER ANSWER: 18.5 BB

TASK w17_4_guided_four_bet_bluff_model [drill] Which scores best, 4-bet with a fold to the all-in or fold now?
CAPTION: CO faces BTN’s 8 BB 3-bet after opening to 2.5 BB. The blinds fold. In 20 equally weighted trial outcomes BTN folds 13 times to a 21 BB 4-bet. In the other seven, BTN goes all-in and CO folds.
TEACH: Which scores best, 4-bet with a fold to the all-in or fold now? The opening raise is sunk. Compare only the 4-bet’s new investment with the current pot.
Q: Which scores best, 4-bet with a fold to the all-in or fold now?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You As 5s | Pot 12 BB | To call 5.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Facts no applicable hand facts
EFFECTIVE: BTN 100
REASONING: principle four_bet_response · alt alternative · edge processRule 1.325 BB · stack_matters false · assumption none
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO As 5s stack 97.5 BB raise 2.5 BB | BTN dealer stack 92 BB raise 8 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB folded stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ folds · preflop: CO raises to 2.5 BB · preflop: BTN raises to 8 BB · preflop: SB folds · preflop: BB folds
  + [correct] 4-bet and fold to the all-in — Correct. 4-bet to 21 BB rather than fold now because BTN folds in 13 of 20 trials. Those pot wins cover the seven new investments lost when BTN goes all-in.
  - [wrong] Fold now — Look again. Folding has zero future cost, while the stated fold rate gives the 4-bet a positive score.
    BETTER ANSWER: 4-bet and fold to the all-in
  - [wrong] Both earn the same — Look again. The total won in fold branches exceeds the total risk lost against all-ins.
    BETTER ANSWER: 4-bet and fold to the all-in

===== WORLD 17 · LESSON traps_and_depth · Traps and depth =====

TASK w17_5_teach [theory] What makes a limp-reraise trap less attractive?
CAPTION: A limp-reraise requires an opponent who raises after the limp. A multiway flop means three or more players see the flop. Deeper stacks leave more postflop money to defend, so compare size and price for the particular positions.
TEACH: What makes a limp-reraise trap less attractive? A limp-reraise requires an opponent who raises after the limp. A multiway flop means three or more players see the flop. Deeper stacks leave more postflop money to defend, so compare size and price for the particular positions.
Q: What makes a limp-reraise trap less attractive?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Players behind usually limp or check as well — Correct. The required raise seldom arrives. A premium hand may see a cheap multiway flop instead.
  - [wrong] An aggressive player raises many limps — Look again. Frequent raises make the intended re-raise opportunity more available.
    BETTER ANSWER: Players behind usually limp or check as well
  - [wrong] You hold a hand eager to play a big pot — Look again. A strong hand can benefit if the trap triggers. You still need that first raise.
    BETTER ANSWER: Players behind usually limp or check as well

===== WORLD 17 · LESSON three_four_bet_checkpoint · Three four bet checkpoint =====

TASK w17_6_teach [theory] Which reason can justify checking back a dry flop in a 3-bet pot?
CAPTION: Preflop re-raises can narrow the ranges and lower SPR. A check-back means checking last after the other players checked. Compare the postflop responses: a check can keep weaker bets available.
TEACH: Which reason can justify checking back a dry flop in a 3-bet pot? Preflop re-raises can narrow the ranges and lower SPR. A check-back means checking last after the other players checked. Compare the postflop responses: a check can keep weaker bets available.
Q: Which reason can justify checking back a dry flop in a 3-bet pot?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] The check retains a weaker group that will bet later — Correct. Compare the later bets with payments you could get immediately and with the chance the free card changes the winner.
  - [wrong] A checked flop in a 3-bet pot signals a trap — Look again. A player may also check a weak or marginal hand. The check alone cannot identify a trap.
    BETTER ANSWER: The check retains a weaker group that will bet later
  - [wrong] A 3-bet forces you to c-bet — Look again. Preflop aggression does not force a postflop wager.
    BETTER ANSWER: The check retains a weaker group that will bet later

===== WORLD 18 · LESSON range_compression · Range compression =====

TASK w18_1_teach [theory] Why can top pair check more often multiway?
CAPTION: Adding a player makes you beat more ranges at showdown. For value, ask which worse hands respond and how often any continuing hand beats yours.
TEACH: Why can top pair check more often multiway? Adding a player makes you beat more ranges at showdown. For value, ask which worse hands respond and how often any continuing hand beats yours.
Q: Why can top pair check more often multiway?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Several ranges can contain stronger hands and worse calls can thin out — Correct. Count the combinations across all active players before adding another bet.
  - [wrong] A third player takes away your pair — Look again. Your card rank remains the same. Its share of the pot can change.
    BETTER ANSWER: Several ranges can contain stronger hands and worse calls can thin out
  - [wrong] A third player prevents value betting — Look again. Strong hands can still collect multiple payments when the response supports them.
    BETTER ANSWER: Several ranges can contain stronger hands and worse calls can thin out

===== WORLD 18 · LESSON joint_fold_threshold · Joint fold threshold =====

TASK w18_2_teach [theory] Which probability prices a pure bluff against two players?
CAPTION: A pure bluff wins immediately only if everyone folds. Conditional frequency means how often a response occurs among the cases where another specified response has occurred. Estimate the joint response directly or use conditional frequencies.
TEACH: Which probability prices a pure bluff against two players? A pure bluff wins immediately only if everyone folds. Conditional frequency means how often a response occurs among the cases where another specified response has occurred. Estimate the joint response directly or use conditional frequencies.
Q: Which probability prices a pure bluff against two players?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] P(first folds) × P(second folds given that fold) — Correct. This is the probability that both players fold in order.
  - [wrong] The average of their separate fold rates — Look again. An average describes neither a joint fold nor a conditional response.
    BETTER ANSWER: P(first folds) × P(second folds given that fold)
  - [wrong] The fold rate of the opponent who acts first — Look again. The second player can still take the pot by continuing.
    BETTER ANSWER: P(first folds) × P(second folds given that fold)

===== WORLD 18 · LESSON position_and_texture · Position and texture =====

TEACH: Who can guarantee a free turn with a check when all earlier players checked? Position lets the last live player close a checking street. ===== WORLD 18 · LESSON reopen_and_limp · Reopen and limp =====

TASK w18_5_teach [theory] How does limping behind differ from overcalling a bet?
CAPTION: The right to raise depends on prior action and the full-raise rule. Limping behind means calling the blind after one or more limps. An overcall matches after another player calls.
TEACH: How does limping behind differ from overcalling a bet? The right to raise depends on prior action and the full-raise rule. Limping behind means calling the blind after one or more limps. An overcall matches after another player calls.
Q: How does limping behind differ from overcalling a bet?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Preflop limpers have only matched the blind. Overcalling follows a bet and call. — Correct. Identify whether a raise or bet was already made and which players paid it.
  - [wrong] Only the position of the next player — Look again. Either action can happen from various seats. The prior contributions supply the definition.
    BETTER ANSWER: Preflop limpers have only matched the blind. Overcalling follows a bet and call.
  - [wrong] The total pot in BB — Look again. The word describes the sequence, not a particular pot.
    BETTER ANSWER: Preflop limpers have only matched the blind. Overcalling follows a bet and call.

===== WORLD 18 · LESSON multiway_checkpoint · Multiway checkpoint =====

TASK w18_6_teach [theory] What extra calculation does a multiway river value bet need?
CAPTION: Before committing multiway, check player order, which holdings continue, and which pot you are eligible to win.
TEACH: What extra calculation does a multiway river value bet need? Before committing multiway, check player order, which holdings continue, and which pot you are eligible to win.
Q: What extra calculation does a multiway river value bet need?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] A showdown share for each set of continuing opponents — Correct. A call from one player differs from calls by both. Their legal holdings cannot share cards.
  - [wrong] The range of just the player who acts first — Look again. The next player may still call and beat that range or yours.
    BETTER ANSWER: A showdown share for each set of continuing opponents
  - [wrong] The sum of the two heads-up equities — Look again. Heads-up shares need not add to the share against both players.
    BETTER ANSWER: A showdown share for each set of continuing opponents
